title: Module 5 Quiz: Building Wealth Over Time

questions.text: How does compound growth impact long-term savings when consistent monthly deposits are maintained over twenty years?
options: It contributes a growing portion of the total balance alongside out-of-pocket deposits.
It caps total growth at a fixed percentage of the initial year's contribution.
It reduces the overall account balance due to administrative fees.
It guarantees that zero market volatility will occur over two decades.
questions.explanation: Over twenty years, compound growth accumulates on top of out-of-pocket contributions, generating an increasing share of the final balance.

questions.text: True or false: Writing a legally binding will ensures property and personal assets are distributed according to the owner's wishes, avoiding court disputes.
questions.explanation: A clear will explicitly outlines asset distribution to help prevent costly court disputes among family members.

questions.text: When constructing a 12-month financial fitness plan, what should be done with a net monthly cash flow surplus?
options: Allocate specific portions toward prioritized financial goals such as emergency savings and debt repayment.
Keep the surplus in a non-interest-bearing cash account without tracking.
Spend the full surplus immediately to prevent lifestyle inflation.
Convert all surplus funds into short-term high-risk investments regardless of debt obligations.
questions.explanation: A monthly surplus should be intentionally assigned toward prioritized goals, including emergency funds, debt reduction, and long-term savings.

questions.text: True or false: Private health, life, and property insurance policies serve to protect personal savings and wealth from major financial disruptions.
questions.explanation: Private insurance policies fill gaps left by basic state benefits, protecting accumulated savings against unexpected major medical or property losses.
